newsitem.title: UK: MCA unable to recommend Scotia's Tarabetic.
newsitem.headline: MCA unable to recommend Scotia's Tarabetic.

text.p: Scotia Holdings Plc said on Tuesday that it has received notification from the Medicines Control Agency (MCA) that it is unable to recommend marketing approval of Scotia's Tarabetic drug.
The British biotechnology firm said it expected to receive a written MCA notice within the next three days.
Scotia said it would ask the Medicines Commission, an advisory body to the MCA, to review Tarabetic and make the final recommendation.
It said it believed that concerns over its drug for diabetic neuropathy related to whether it is efficacious in both insulin and non-insulin dependent diabetes.
Scotia also believes there are concerns whether there is evidence of efficacy if two of the twelve trial centres are excluded from analysis.
"The board of Scotia is confident that it is in a position to respond favourably to these issues," said the company in a statement.
Scotia noted that Epogam, its drug for atopic eczema, was delayed in a similar way but then approved for marketing in the UK in 1988.
By 0955 GMT, shares in the company had crashed 135p to stand at 435p on the back of the announcement.
